claim: Effect MCP HTTP stores header names lowercase: mcp-protocol-version, mcp-method, mcp-name, mcp-session-id.

A 2026-07-28 HTTP POST must send MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, and (for tools/call, prompts/get, resources/read) Mcp-Name matching the JSON-RPC body, or Effect returns HTTP 400 HeaderMismatch (-32020).
Sidecar /mcp CORS allowedHeaders are authorization, content-type, mcp-protocol-version, mcp-session-id. Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name are absent; exposedHeaders are mcp-protocol-version and mcp-session-id.

A browser-origin client of /mcp under a 2026-07-28-only server cannot complete CORS preflight: setting Mcp-Method (and Mcp-Name on tool/resource/prompt calls) is non-simple and those names are not in allowedHeaders. In-repo HttpClient tests do not exercise preflight.
2026-07-28 ignores Mcp-Session-Id: a request carrying it still succeeds and the response does not mint or echo a session id.

Effect layerHttp accepts only POST with Content-Type application/json (else 415) and Accept listing both application/json and text/event-stream (else 406). GET/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/OPTIONS are 405 Allow: POST when Origin is allowed, and 403 empty when Origin is present and not listed.

Effect Origin check allows missing Origin and default-denies any present Origin not in allowedOrigins. Sidecar Origin middleware denies missing Origin (O.exists) and answers attacker Origin POST with typed JSON 403 OntologyMcpOriginForbidden. Same five-origin allowlist is also passed to layerHttp.

Sidecar CORS short-circuits OPTIONS to HTTP 204. For a disallowed Origin that 204 has no Access-Control-Allow-Origin (only Vary: Origin). Spec and Effect security tests require 403 for attacker Origin on OPTIONS. Sidecar comment claims every OPTIONS is 204 before the route handler; no in-repo OPTIONS test exists.

G9 stdio hosts (nlp, m365, uspto, gov-legal, law-practice/practice-kg) use layerStdio only and have no Origin, CORS, or HTTP method surface. Desktop HTTP MCP mounts only when BEEP_DESKTOP_RPC_SESSION_TOKEN is set; IPC never mounts it.

Effect layerHttp does not authenticate, rate-limit, or cap body size; surrounding server must bind and install auth. Sidecar binds 127.0.0.1, requires a per-launch bearer on non-OPTIONS, and has no request-size cap or rate limiter on /mcp.

Without MCP sessions, replay of a captured /mcp POST is limited only by the static per-launch bearer, the Origin allowlist (browsers), and process lifetime. Effect 2026-07-28 ignores Mcp-Session-Id and provides no request nonce.

Sidecar MCP observability today: spans ontology.mcp.origin (decision, method), desktop.rpc.authorize (decision, method), mcp.tool.call.${name} (parameters sanitized), McpServer / McpServer/Notifications / McpServer/Client prefixes; counters desktop_ontology_mcp_origin_decisions_total and desktop_rpc_auth_decisions_total; warn logs on origin/auth deny without logging Origin values or the bearer.

sanitizedToolkit still reads mcp-session-id into McpCallerIdentity.sessionId. Under 2026-07-28 HTTP the server does not mint that header, so sessionId is None unless a client supplies one. A client-supplied value is unauthenticated: Effect ignores it for routing but the kit and GovernedTierGate would still key a run on it.

On HTTP, RpcServer clientId increments per request. With sessionId None, GovernedTierGate runIdOf becomes client:${clientId} per POST, so ledger chains and grant freeze cannot span two tools/call posts. Stdio clientIds is Set([0]), so stdio run identity stays process-scoped.

Spans never attached mcp-session-id; OTEL resource session_id is BEEP_QA_SESSION_ID. The join across origin/auth/tool/ledger today is the MCP session header (HTTP) or client:0 (stdio). G4 HTTP loses that join unless a new correlation key is chosen.

Current sidecar protocol pin is v2025_06_18 only. A G4 v2026_07_28-only flip is unimplementable for browser-origin /mcp clients unless CORS allowedHeaders grow mcp-method and mcp-name, and it breaks the in-repo harness that still POSTs initialize and captures mcp-session-id.

MCP 2026-07-28 MAY mirror tool parameters into Mcp-Param-* when x-mcp-header is set; Effect validates those headers against the body. beep-effect tool schemas do not use x-mcp-header today. If they ever do, sidecar CORS must allow Mcp-Param-* or browser clients fail.

Stateful HTTP echoes MCP-Protocol-Version on responses via a session pre-response handler that runs only when prepared.binding is defined. Stateless admission sets binding undefined, and 2026-07-28 conformance does not assert a protocol-version response header.

Default-deny Origin in Effect is empty allowedOrigins: any present Origin is 403 unless the caller passed a list. Origin-less non-browser clients remain valid. Spec requires 403 only when Origin is present and invalid.

Keeping a mixed protocol list (stateful + one stateless) on the sidecar would preserve mcp-session-id minting, CORS expose of that header, and GovernedTierGate HTTP run chaining. Effect permits mixed lists with at most one stateless adapter. That option contradicts working assumption G4.
